evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi online text, 姐 entry
evidence.field: 卷十二·女部·姐; entry and Duan Yucai note
evidence.text: The entry reports that Shu people called a mother 姐 and Huainan people called her 社; it analyzes 姐 as 女 plus phonetic 且 and gives “read like 左.” Duan Yucai says the term is regional, suggests the graph was made by Shu speakers, and notes 社 and 姐 are close in sound. This supports the traditional component analysis and preserves it as an old dictionary account, not independent proof of the first graphic form or the whole word’s semantic history.
evidence.title: 說文解字「姐」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00906 姐; form analysis and senses
evidence.text: The entry repeats Shuowen’s 女 plus phonetic 且 analysis and specifies how the modern written form’s 且 component is shaped. It cites Song-dynasty Hong Mai, Yijian yizhi, for “大姐” in a sibling-age context; Yuan-dynasty Guan Hanqing, Saving the Dusty, uses 姐姐 for an older woman; and a Yuan song uses 姐儿 for a young woman. These are later documented uses, but the cited examples do not show a continuous change from the Shuowen regional ‘mother’ term.
evidence.title: A00906 姐 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Xiao Xu, Fudan Center for Research on Chinese Excavated Texts
evidence.field: discussion of 淮南謂母曰社; cited lexical traditions
evidence.text: The article collects parallel mother-address terms/forms such as 姐/社, 媞, 姼, 毑, 她 and 恀, with differing scholarly explanations. It records dispute over whether some forms are phonetic records, related forms, or separate words. Its compilation does not establish one derivational chain or a transition from ‘mother’ to ‘elder sister.’
evidence.title: 蕭旭：《淮南子》古楚語舉證

evidence.field: Summary, source, permission, licensing, file history
evidence.text: The file description identifies the image as a digitally created Shuowen seal-script-style rendering of 姐, links its source record to hanziyuan S09148, and gives a public-domain release for this representation. The file history records its SVG creation in 2014. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact.

This local dataset therefore cannot supply a same-system reconstruction comparison for host and component. Do not combine these Baxter–Sagart forms with Zhengzhang’s reconstruction of 姐.

evidence.text: The local full reading file contains kMandarin jiě for 姐 (U+59D0) and qiě for 且 (U+4E14). These are current metadata only and do not establish an ancient sound relationship. The tracked HSK1 extract also contains 姐 as jiě (row 145); it does not cover 且. The required official Unicode GetUnihanData pages for both code points returned access errors in this run, so the local readings lack a verified official per-character click-through here.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese 姐 entry (secondary reconstruction attribution)
evidence.field: Old Chinese phonetic series; reconstructions attributed to Zhengzhang Shangfang
evidence.text: The page reports Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *ʔsjaːʔ for 姐 and *sʰjaːʔ, *ʔsa for 且. The similar sound material is consistent with the proposed phonetic role, but the page is a secondary compilation, and multiple 且 readings are reported. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV has no 姐 row, so the two reconstruction systems cannot be directly reconciled from this local dataset.

gaps: No visually inspected early artifact form or secure excavated attestation for 姐 was found. Available sources support the Shuowen seal-script tradition but leave earlier graphic history and possible corruption unresolved.

The Shuowen reports a regional ‘mother’ use. Song and Yuan citations attest sibling-age, older-woman, and young-woman uses, but no evidence here establishes when or how the semantic relation developed; graph borrowing versus semantic change remains unresolved.

The source word or object behind 且 was not established in this research and is unnecessary for the directly attested claim that Shuowen treats 且 as a phonetic component in 姐. No whole-graph loan claim is supported.
Current Mandarin readings are recorded locally as 姐 jiě and 且 qiě, but official Unicode per-character pages were inaccessible. Do not treat current readings as evidence for ancient phonetic function.

The local Baxter–Sagart data has 且 entries but no 姐 row found, preventing direct host/component comparison within that system. Zhengzhang values are secondary-source reports and must not be merged with Baxter–Sagart notation.

Xiaoxuetang's query interface rendered as a shell without surfaced form labels/images in this browsing tool, so no Xiaoxuetang candidate was selected. Commons' seal file is a digital reconstruction, not an artifact photograph.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; conventionally associated with the late Warring States/Qin standardization and transmitted in the Han dictionary tradition; this is a modern digital redraw, not a dated artifact
items.tradition: Chinese small seal-script style, identified by Commons as Shuowen seal script
items.caption: A modern redraw of 姐 in the Shuowen seal-script style. The dictionary analyzes it as 女 plus phonetic 且; this image illustrates that transmitted analysis, not an excavated early form.
items.alt: Digital vector rendering of the seal-script form of 姐, showing a 女-like left component and 且-like right component.
items.selection_reason: It is a well-documented and reusable rendering matching the only clearly supported early graphic tradition found in accessible sources. Use as an illustrative reconstruction, not as proof of an oracle-bone or bronze form.
items.rights: Public domain release stated on the Wikimedia Commons file page; attribution appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: The seal-style candidate is a modern digital reconstruction derived from character databases, not a photograph or independently dated artifact; no earlier excavated 姐 glyph was established in the inspected sources.
Exact Unicode Unihan pages could not be inspected, and Xiaoxuetang's queried record rendered only a shell without candidate labels or images in this browsing tool.
